frenchVerbParadigms.englishExplanation: Irregular. The singular forms are comprends, comprends, comprend. The plural stem changes: compren- in nous comprenons and vous comprenez, and comprenn- in ils/elles comprennent. 'Je ne comprends pas' = 'I don't understand.'

Irregular. The stem is peu- in the singular (peux, peux, peut), pouv- for nous and vous (pouvons, pouvez), and peuv- in ils/elles peuvent. 'Pouvez-vous...?' is the present tense with vous and means 'Can you...?'; use it to ask a server politely, as in 'Pouvez-vous parler plus lentement, s'il vous plaît ?'
Regular -er verb. 'Parler plus lentement' = 'to speak more slowly'. After pouvez-vous, the verb stays in the infinitive: 'Pouvez-vous parler...?'

Irregular. Use it to say what something is or what it is made of: 'Les ingrédients sont des tortillas, de la salsa verde, du poulet et du fromage.' ('The ingredients are tortillas, green salsa, chicken and cheese.'). 'Quels sont les ingrédients ?' also uses sont, because the subject is plural.

Irregular. Je shortens to j' before a vowel, so the first form is j'ai, never 'je ai'. 'Emma a une réservation' = 'Emma has a reservation.' The fixed expression il y a ('there is / there are') is built from avoir (il + y + a), as in 'il y a des informations d'urgence'.

internalDomainNotes: Source authority: the English source text is the parity anchor. The French translates it and does not replace it. Every English string in forms and modes is the exact source English; any English change must come from the owner.

Place facts kept from the source: Café Luna, a reservation at 9, emergency information on the wall in English and Spanish, chilaquiles with chicken, the ingredient list (tortillas, green salsa, chicken and cheese), and a vegetarian option with a variety of vegetables. The source gives no city, so none is added.
Drift not used: Lyon, Café Lumière, French signage, ham quiche, tartine, pastry and eggs are not in this candidate.

Card 12: the source English is 'How do you say this in Spanish?', so the French is 'Comment dit-on ça en espagnol ?'. Both sides of the card now say the same thing. The 'en français' adaptation is not applied; it is an owner decision (see residuals).

Salsa verde: the source 'green salsa' is the Mexican tomatillo-based salsa served with chilaquiles. The French keeps the loanword 'salsa verde'. 'Sauce verte' is not used, because in French it names a different sauce (a French herb sauce).

Can you: the source uses present 'puede' and English 'Can you', so the French is present 'Pouvez-vous'. This matches the vous form in the pouvoir paradigm. The conditional 'Pourriez-vous' ('Could you') is not used.
Cognate endings: the Spanish focus (-ción, -dad, -ente) corresponds to French -tion (réservation, information, option), -té (spécialité, variété) and -ent (ingrédient, différent, excellent).

Gender and agreement: la réservation, l'information, la spécialité, la variété, l'option and l'urgence are feminine; les ingrédients is masculine plural. So the reader has 'est différente' (spécialité), 'est excellente' (option), 'une urgence' and 'Quels sont les ingrédients ?'.
Register: Emma addresses Rosa with vous ('Excusez-moi', 'Pouvez-vous'). 'Comment dit-on' is neutral and fits the same register.

Speaking: the source speaking line has exactly three tasks (say you don't understand, ask the server to speak more slowly, ask what the ingredients of the specialty are). The speaking objectives contain only these three. The vegetarian-option and emergency phrases remain as cards and reader lines but are not speaking tasks.

Emergency content: the source states no emergency number, so none is given anywhere in this candidate and none appears in learner-facing objectives. 'Au secours, c'est une urgence !' is kept only as the translation of source card 15.
Hear mode: the hear item now uses card 11 instead of reader line 5, so the audio prompt has no 'Emma :' speaker label for text-to-speech to read aloud.

Formatting: French lines use a regular space before ':', '?' and '!'. The English keeps the source 'Emma:' and 'Rosa:' with no space. forms and modes quote the French and English strings exactly as they appear in frenchCards, frenchReader and the source.

speakingSourceEnglish: Tell a server you don't understand, ask them to speak more slowly, and ask what the ingredients of the specialty are.
speakingObjectives: Scene: Emma arrives for her 9 o'clock reservation at Café Luna. Roles: the learner is Emma, Rosa is the server. Task 1: Tell Rosa you don't understand: 'Excusez-moi, je ne comprends pas.'
Task 2: Ask Rosa to speak more slowly: 'Pouvez-vous parler plus lentement, s'il vous plaît ?'
Task 3: Ask what the ingredients of today's specialty (the chilaquiles with chicken) are: 'Quels sont les ingrédients ?'
